Title: How Do Early Childhood Education Pre-service Teachers view Science and Scientists?
Journal: The Eurasia Proceedings of Educational and Social Sciences
Description: The aim of this case study was to collect and to assess students’ views about their NOS understandings at the beginning and at the end of their course on teaching science. The study was conducted on 24 students, all females, in their 3rd semester (2nd year), enrolled in their initial teacher education program in early childhood education. Data were collected from 1) Draw-a-scientist-at-task tool, 2) pre- and post-questionnaires about students’ views about science and scientists and 3) students’ formative and summative assessment scores. To increase the validity of results, a member checking was used. Results showed that prospective teachers’ views about NOS improved significantly after attending only one course and the that majority of students agreed on the importance of learning more about science for their professional development.

Description: The Faculty of Education is currently in the phase of revising its LMD programs. In order to modernize and to keep in track with the latest trends in Education, the Science and Math department made an in-depth study that involves 30 teachers and 9 trainers, who presented their ideas for innovation, suggestions for new courses and improvement in the present courses.  A large scale survey was done on undergraduate students, in order to collect ideas about the taught courses, students’ skills and courses learning outcomes, as well as needs and suggestions for new courses. Qualitative and quantitative data were collected a) from 1005 students-filled questionnaires that assess 33 courses from the Science and Mathematics Department and lasted over 6 semesters, as well as practicum courses at schools and b) a focus group of 34 students, in their last semester, filled a questionnaire detailing the taught courses, new courses and comments about their learning during their 6 semesters at the Faculty. Teachers suggested new courses like STEM and science and industry, proposed new specializations, such as science and math teacher preparation for middle classes, and redistribute some current courses. Students in their last semester, for instance, were satisfied with the taught courses related to their specialization, they complained from the redundancy in some courses like psychology and general education and they emphasize on taking into consideration their opinions and suggestions in the assessment of the LMD program.

Title: Lebanese Public Schools Principals’ Attitudes, Level of ICT Use and Leadership Style
Journal: The Eurasia Proceedings of Educational and Social Sciences
Authors: Suzanne El Takach, Zalpha Ayoubı, İbrahim Kıbbı
Description: The purpose of this study was to investigate attitudes towards ICT, level of ICT use, and leadership style of the Lebanese public schools’ attending a training program at the Lebanese University, Faculty of Education. The training program, in which 204 principals from all over Lebanon participated, lasted for three months. At the end of the program, they filled a survey questionnaire and only 192 filled-in the questionnaire. Data collected were analyzed using descriptive analysis and correlations were calculated to identify the relationships between ICT use and gender, age, number of computers at school, earned Diploma, geographical location. School principals agreed that they benefit greatly from the ICT course; it helped them in improving their computer skills relevant to their administrative work. Findings also suggest that there is a no significant correlation between the use of ICT and school principal gender and age, the good equipment of schools is irrelevant with the school geographical location (urban/rural city). Moreover, within this study, the researchers identify significant challenges faced by the trainees’ school principals, for instance, the little number and the lack of computers in their schools, the absence of IT teachers and even many of them did not use often computers in their daily routine works before the training program. Finally, Lebanese school principals adopted an administrative style with an emphasis on the accountable management behavior. Future qualitative studies are recommended to gain in-depth knowledge about the use of ICT by school principals in their schools.

Title: Using drawings to investigate Lebanese in-service science teachers’ views on teaching and learning process
Authors: Suzanne El Takach, Zalpha Ayoubi, Muhammad Rawas
Description: The aim of this study was to explore Lebanese in-service science teachers’ views on teaching and learning science. The study was conducted using a qualitative method design. The participants included 41 in-service cycle 3 chemistry teachers, in the Lebanese public schools all over Lebanon, who attended a training program at the Faculty of Education, Lebanese University. Teachers’ drawings about their views on teaching and learning in science were collected using the “Draw-About-Science-Teaching-and-Learning” or DASTL. Data from drawings were coded and categorized using 15 indicators related to teacher, student and learning environment. Results showed that initially most in-service science teachers held a traditional behavioristic view about teaching and learning where the teacher is in charge of the teaching/learning process and that knowledge is transmitted from the teacher to his passive students through the only chalk-and-talk instruction. In the postquestionnaire, most teachers presented more emphasis on the learning environment, a smiling teacher whose role is to create an engaging environment to students. Post-drawings represented more studentcentered methods as the laboratory and discussion. Finally, teachers’ views have changed from the behaviorist towards more constructivist teaching practices. Teachers emphasized the use of active teaching strategies such as the use of group work and technology.

Title: A Case Study on Pre-service Science Teachers’ Assessment of Some Teaching Science Courses at the Faculty of Education, Lebanese University
Description: The present case study examined pre-service teachers’ attitudes towards 6 courses taught in 3rd till 6th semesters at the Lebanese University, the Faculty of Education, during the academic year 2016-2017. They also assessed science teaching courses that are essential for preparing future teachers to teach science to primary and elementary pupils. These courses were: Action Research I and II in Teaching Science, New trends in Teaching Science, Teaching Science I and II. All of those courses are taken by pre-service teachers majoring in elementary science education, and Teaching Science for Early Childhood Education, recently referred to as primary education. Qualitative and Quantitative Data were gathered from a) a survey questionnaire consisting of 16 items; some were of Likert scale type that aimed at collecting students’ opinions on courses, in terms of teaching, assessment and class environment. The sample consisted of 67 pre-service teachers, who filled 105 questionnaires and b) pre-service science and mathematics teachers’ reflections (N= 35) in their last semester in Science and Mathematics, in order to know more about their opinions of teaching science courses for teacher preparation at the Faculty of Education, their skills gained and for improving the present curriculum of science education. Pre-service teachers were satisfied with science teaching courses and they have admitted that they gained a good pedagogical content knowledge, such as, lesson planning, use of various teaching and assessment strategies, and how to do action research in a science class.

Authors: Suzanne El Takach, Ibrahim Kibbi, Zalpha Ayoubi
Description: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has improved the quality of our daily activities and it is currently used in almost all professions. The purpose of this article is to study seven science teachers’ attitudes and their students’(N= 228) towards ICT and how ICT is actually used in their classroom practices. The teachers under study were teaching Physics, Chemistry and Biology for the middle school which is a private school located in Beirut area. To do so, a) we designed and we asked these in-service teachers to fill-in attitudes checklists, b) we designed and filled-in classroom observations logs. The classroom teaching sessions were videotaped and analyzed using an observation log and c) after each teaching session, students had to fill in an attitude checklist.{N= 100 for English students and N= 128 for French students}. Data validation was in-depth data interpretation, data triangulation and peer review. The main outcomes of the study were: delivery of science to students depends on teacher’ICT skills, class interaction improves with ICT-enhanced science instruction as well as students’ learning outcomes improved. More studies on larger samples need to be undergone in order to generalize these findings.

Authors: Ibrahim Kibbi, Suzanne El Takach, Zalpha Ayoubi
Description:
The role of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in school classrooms is becoming prominent due to the potential value of such technologies as tools for learning and to its importance in enhancing the teaching and learning process. But, several challenges emerged for learners and teachers. This study examined the science prospective teachers’ attitudes towards ICT as well as the efficacy of the training course given at the Faculty of Education, Lebanese University. A pre-and post-questionnaires were distributed among 75 science teachers enrolled in CAPES. A follow-up phone survey was done after one year to track these teachers during instruction.
The findings suggest that ICT professional development courses for teacher were helping them to improve their ICT skills and knowledge. Findings also revealed that the majority of science teachers have a positive attitude towards ICT with several factors affecting this improvement and integration in schools: limited infrastructural facilities and the lack of appropriate teacher development at schools. The most important recommendation is to ensure the use of interactive boards in classes; E-learning as well as mobile and IPad learning. It is hoped that the outcomes of this study can be used in shaping innovational practices in the Lebanese Educational System.
